headline.text: Grain elevators and port terminals held 7.25 million tonnes of grain in the week ending 4 October 2026. That is higher than at this time of year in any of the past five years. It is about 2% above the typical level. Worth watching. One unusual reading does not mean a crisis.

Ports shipped 3.21 million tonnes of grain abroad in the four weeks to 4 October 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 4% above the typical level.

We follow 12 fresh fruits and vegetables at the Toronto wholesale market. In the latest week, two cost more and two cost less than at this time of year in any recent year, after allowing for inflation. Four are in their normal range, and for four we do not have enough past data.
In October 2026, grocery prices were 2.0% higher than a year earlier, and average hourly wages were 2.2% higher. Wages have risen faster than grocery prices for two months in a row.

The Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System, run by the United Nations and the European Commission, lists eight serious disasters around the world. Four are in countries Canada buys food or farm supplies from. That tells us where to look; it does not mean Canada is affected.

happening.title: Weather warnings
happening.text: 11 weather alerts were in effect in four provinces or territories when we last checked, including five warnings.

happening.title: Food recalls
happening.text: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency issued 21 food recall notices in the 30 days to 20 November 2026. That is normal for this time of year: it is within the range of the past five years. It is about 12% below the typical level.

happening.title: Disasters abroad
happening.text: Eight serious disasters listed worldwide in recent weeks; four in countries that supply Canada.

happening.title: Government announcements
happening.text: 11 announcements about food or farming from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency or Public Safety Canada in the last 30 days.

reach.title: Tropical Cyclone MURASU-26
reach.text: India supplied 27% of the rice Canada imported in 2025, and one other product we track. India is a large country, so the disaster may be far from where these are grown.

reach.title: Earthquake in China
reach.text: China supplied 7% of the crustaceans (incl. shrimp) Canada imported in 2025. China is a large country, so the disaster may be far from where these are grown.

questions.text: There is more grain in storage than in any recent year at this time. Is that a comfortable reserve, or grain waiting for trains and ships?

Wholesale prices for strawberries from the United States and peppers from Ontario are higher than in any recent year at this time. Is the cause weather where they are grown, the exchange rate, or something else?

scenario_of_week.title: A cyberattack takes a grocery distributor offline
scenario_of_week.reason: no reading this week points to one threat in particular, so we feature a different one each week
